sentence: No past light cone of an exterior event meets $\mathcal{H}^+$. A point $x$ in the closure of $J^-(O(\tau))$ has $I^-(x)\subseteq I^-(O(\tau))$, on which $\Theta<\Theta(O(\tau))$; if $x$ lay on $\mathcal{H}^+$, a past-directed timelike curve from $x$ would lie in $I^-(x)\subseteq D$ and be future-inextendible in $D$, so by the Cauchy property $\Theta$ would grow without bound along it, which it cannot. So neither $J^-(O(\tau))$ nor its boundary meets $\mathcal{H}^+$.
